segments.text: For a long time, I thought my problem with faith was simply not believing good enough.
Now I understand it was the conditions that I allowed myself to live in.
Welcome to Life is Your Word, in this show we understand reality by seeking God first.
We're currently going through a mini-series on the fruit of the Spirit, and today's fruit patience.
Today's reading will be from Luke 8.
Jesus set a parable. A sower went out to sow the seed. Some fell on the path
and was trampled on. Some fell on rock and it grew up and withered for lack of
whisper. Some among thorns and the thorns choked it and yet some fell on good
soil. And when it grew, it produced a hundredfold. The parable means this. The seed is God's
word. Those on the path have heard. Those on the path have heard the word but the devil
takes it away. But the devil takes it away from their hearts so they don't believe. The ones in the rocks
hear the word, receive it with joy, but have no root. They've in testing, they fall away. Those in
the thorns are choked by the cares and riches of life and their fruit does not mature. But for the good
soil, these are the ones when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart and bear fruit
with endurance.

I grew up in the church and I heard all about God's word, and I knew it well. I read the Bible multiple times in high school, but my life was crowded, trying to pursue things that I thought were good, but in reality were selfish desires.
I felt pressure, I felt fear, I was trying to survive instead of being formed by God.
So the word kept getting choked out, so my fruit couldn't mature, so the word couldn't take root and my fruit couldn't mature.
But Jesus never blames the seed. There doesn't mean there's anything wrong with the seed itself. The word is still good. He points to the soil and soil can change.
Patience only came not because I was trying not because I learned how to wait
better but because I started tending to my own life making space letting
God work deeper than my urgency allowing growth to take time instead of
forcing results. Patience was not the goal. Patience was the fruit. It showed
up when the word was finally allowed to stay long enough to grow and produce
good fruit. The seed was always alive what changed was my life the soil that
it grew in. Patience has never been about waiting but about becoming a place
where life can fully form.
How has God taught you about patience?
Share your revelations in the comments.
In love and unity, Acebele.
